summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Teramoto studied at Kumbum Monastery in 1903. He held posts as lecturer at Kyoto University (~1908–1923) and professor at Otani University in 1915.

Working in Buddhist studies, Ocho studied at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1931) under Daijo Tokiwa. He was a researcher at the Academy of Oriental Culture in 1931 and served as professor emeritus at Otani University (1949–1976).

Specializing in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Inoue studied at Higashi Hongan-ji and the University of Tokyo under Ernest Francisco Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara. He founded Toyo University, serving as a lecturer and manager (~1887–1905).

A specialist in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Kanakura earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tohoku University (1923–1929) and Rissho University (~1959–1974), and became president of Miyagi University of Education in 1967.
A Buddhist studies scholar, Nasu completed a PhD at Ryukoku University (attested 1996) under doctoral supervisor Esho Mikogami and also studied under Kei Mikogami.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Kurumiya completed a Ph.D. at the Australian National University by 1974. He held a post as professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University (attested 1981–1985).

Lo Bue specialized in Tibetology and earned his Ph.D. at SOAS University of London (~1975–1981). He was a lecturer in Tibetan language and literature at the University of Milan (~1983–2002) and held a post at the University of Bologna (~2002–2016).

Mortensen, a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies, completed his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2003) under supervisors Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton, alongside several other teachers.

Specializing in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics, Grinstead studied at Victoria University of Wellington (~1945–1950). He held posts at the British Library (~1957–1970) and the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies (1969).
Huntington is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Gary A. Tubb.

Specializing in religious studies and Indology, Sharpe studied at Manchester under Samuel George Frederick Brandon and earned a doctorate from Uppsala University. He held posts at Lancaster, Uppsala, and the University of Sydney as First Chair of Religious Studies (1977–1996).

A scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Greene earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf. He served as assistant professor of religious studies at Yale University (attested 2017).
A scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, Reinders studied under mentors Allan G. Grapard and William F. Powell.

A Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar, Goodell studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Virginia, completing an MA and studying under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner (attested 2012).
A scholar in Tibetology and Sinology, Teichman completed his studies at Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge between ~1903 and 1906.

Specializing in Japanology and religious studies, Baffelli studied under Massimo Raveri (~2002–2006). She held academic posts at the University of Otago (~2009–2013) and the University of Manchester (~2013, 2018).

Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Frauwallner completed his doctorate at the University of Vienna. He held multiple appointments there, serving in Indology (1928–1929), as director (1938, 1942), and as professor (1955–1964).

A scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology, Haenisch studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Wilhelm Grube. He held professorships at Leipzig (~1925–1932), Berlin (1932), Munich (1927–1951), and Göttingen (1925).

Heintel was a philosophy scholar who completed his Dr. phil. and Habilitation at the University of Vienna. He held posts there as extraordinary professor (1952) and ordinary professor of philosophy (1960–1982).

A scholar of philosophy, Jaensch completed his PhD at Göttingen and Habilitation at Strasbourg. He served as professor of philosophy at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1912–1913) and ordinary professor at the University of Marburg (1913).
